guidance.summary: For full-year 2026, MIAX lowered its adjusted operating expense guidance to $260-$270 million and raised its share-based compensation and depreciation and amortization ranges, while keeping capital expenditures ($40-$45 million) and the adjusted effective tax rate (27%-29%) unchanged.

guidance.sentence: • Adjusted operating expenses, which exclude share-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, and litigation expenses, in a range between $260 million and $270 million, down from previous guidance of between $265 million and $275 million;
• Share-based compensation expense in a range between $29 million and $32 million, up from previous guidance of between $27 million and $30 million;
• Capital expenditures, including capitalization of internally developed software, in a range between $40 million and $45 million, unchanged from previous guidance;
• Depreciation and amortization expense in a range between $35 million and $39 million, up from previous guidance of between $33 million and $38 million;
• Adjusted effective tax rate post valuation allowance release in a range between 27% and 29%, unchanged from previous guidance.

writeup.headline: MIAX rates Hold: solid growth, net cash and low absolute multiples offset by a very weak share price trend.
writeup.thesis: MIAX scores 59, a Hold, 6 points below the Buy band. Growth is a strength, with TTM revenue growth of 16.8% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 18.3% year on year, and growth sped up by 5.2 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet scores 100 thanks to net cash, and valuation scores 80 on low absolute levels: P/S of 2.2x, P/FCF of 12.6x and an FCF yield 2.9 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield; there is no comparison with its own history. Holding the score back are quality at 48, with a 7.9% operating margin and diluted share count up 41.1% year on year, and a trend score of just 2, with the price 43.7% below its 52-week high and shares 42.0 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days.
key_risks: Heavy dilution: diluted share count up 41.1% year on year
Thin operating margin of 7.9% and gross margin of 34.4%
Weak momentum, with the price 22.9% below its 200-day average and shares down 23.5% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago
Three brokers cut price targets, and KBW said Q3 volumes missed its estimates
Q3 2026 results due after the close on 2026-10-29 could disappoint on revenue capture
what_would_change: A 6-point rise in the score would reach Buy, most plausibly from a recovering share price trend (currently scored 2)
Better margins or slower dilution lifting the quality score from 48 would also help
A fall of more than 15 points, such as growth stalling or valuation losing its appeal, would push it to Sell
Weak Q3 results or guidance could lower the growth and news risk scores
